sources.supports: Identifies the Inland Ice as the continental ice sheet and explains the map representation of surface elevation, ice thickness and sub-ice bedrock contours. Its register locates Danmark Fjord and Mylius-Erichsen Land without identifying this modeled route as a named river.
sources.limits: General glaciology and a map-label register cannot establish a name for the complete modeled river group. No present-day ice dimensions, margin position or melt-rate estimate is inferred from this historical report.

correspondence: Piece 9207 follows the western feeder/lake corridor southward and then turns northeast within the broad Lac Joseph setting. Piece 9208 continues southeast through the connecting lake-and-channel chain toward the western Atikonak Lake approach. The retained Quebec sheet supplies the water outlines and graticule for this entire southwestern context but does not print the needed local river names. Nalcor's hydrological account independently places Lac Joseph upstream of Atikonak Lake. No name is invented for the initial feeder or every connecting reach.

Piece 9209 proceeds north through the Atikonak Lake outlet corridor, past the independently located Atikonak River above Panchia Lake station, and into the southeastern Ossokmanuan lake/reservoir corridor. Its later eastward and northward bend follows the Unknown River/Twin Falls outlet toward Churchill. DFO Figure 1 separately labels Unknown River and shows the Ossokmanuan outlet relationship; it does not call this river Churchill.

Nalcor's 2009 hydrological sequence distinguishes normal Ossokmanuan outflow through Gabbro into Smallwood from the Ossokmanuan control-structure spill route through the former Twin Falls site into Churchill. The selected model follows the latter corridor. It must not be described as the ordinary present-day operational flow route through Smallwood, nor as proof of current discharge through every modeled reach.

Piece 9210 follows the mapped lower Churchill corridor east from the Unknown River junction region, through the long Winokapau Lake passage, the southward valley bend, Gull Island and Muskrat Falls vicinity, and the outlet beside Happy Valley-Goose Bay. The readable Nalcor two-page map shows this sequence and directly labels Churchill River. The named river's Smallwood-to-Lake Melville relationship is also stated by the provincial flood-warning page.

The wider group includes separate northwestern and northern lake/tributary corridors in the Menihek–Smallwood setting and shorter central tributary approaches. The retained Quebec sheet, DFO reservoir map and provincial description provide representative surrounding-system context. MAIN_RIV membership and the modeled mainstem classification do not establish identical names for those separate branches; no attempt is made to name all 16 fragments.

correspondence.finding: All three actual cached pieces were inspected together and individually against readable graticules, complete IGN physical sheets and enlarged corridor portions. The correspondence used the north–south upper valley, eastward bend south of Tinogasta, southeast passage below Pipanaco, southward turn through the Llanos, southern U-shaped bend and final northeastward salt-flat traverse; neither the bounding box nor MAIN_RIV was used as a river-name assignment.

The northern headwater approaches the eastern upper branch of the mapped Fiambalá valley and continues south along the corridor labeled Río Fiambalá o Saujil. The exact northernmost modeled extension and its local headwater name remain unresolved. IGN separately shows Chaschuil/Guanchín approaching from the west and Río Grande from the east; those tributary names are not transferred to the selected northern branch.

Farther south the route follows IGN’s Río Abaucán, passes the Tinogasta corridor and turns east beneath the Sierras de Copacabana and Vinquis, then southeast along the river printed Río Salado o Colorado south of Salar de Pipanaco. INA’s 2010 description directly sets out the Fiambalá–Abaucán naming sequence and the Tinogasta/El Salado turns. Precise name-change points are not fixed by these generalized sources.

After the southeast bend, the selected line turns south through the Mazán corridor east of Sierra de Velasco. The La Rioja sheet labels this Río Salado o Colorado and shows its southern weakening/termination at Desagües del Río Salado. The federal basin description places loss by infiltration near Cebollar. The 2018 glacier-inventory basin figure covers the upper route and a southeastern basin tail, but does not establish a named river continuing to Salinas Grandes.

The southern end of 14003 and the beginning of 14004 lie beyond the IGN sheet’s printed Desagües del Río Salado, in the northern Salina La Antigua setting. Piece 14004 proceeds south along that salt-flat corridor, bends east south of 30°S, then reaches the western Salinas Grandes setting. IGN labels La Antigua and Salinas Grandes as salt flats and does not draw or name a continuous river matching this whole connector. This does not prove that all ephemeral drainage or occasional flow connections are absent.

The final piece continues east and then northeast across the Salinas Grandes setting toward its eastern side. The Catamarca sheet covers this complete eastern extension and labels the salt flat, but provides no river name for the modeled traverse. Salinas Grandes is therefore geographical/feature-class context, not a candidate river name.

The regional maps separately label Río Bermejo o Vinchina west of the route, Río Belén and Salar de Pipanaco east of the upper valley, and Río Paganzo o Colorado and Desagües de Los Colorados farther southwest of the lower extension. In particular, the Colorado name on the Paganzo drainage is not the selected Salado/Colorado corridor. No adjacent river or salt-flat name is applied to the entire group.

correspondence.object_scope: Both actual cached modeled mainstem pieces were read over the complete displayed route, including the short northeastern terminal piece. The bounding box and the earlier Greenland target were not substituted for this path.
correspondence.displayed_length_limit: Retained model display length, not an independently established natural-river length.
correspondence.full_path_finding: The long western northward leg, its northern bend and the eastward interior reaches lie on the mapped Inland Ice. The later eastward and northward approach reaches the ice-margin and ice-free terrain south of Mylius-Erichsen Land; the final short piece approaches inner Danmark Fjord. Both pieces were considered against the readable northern graticule, ice shading, mapped margin and fjord/land outline.
correspondence.map_interpretation: Blue surface contours, dashed ice-thickness isopachs and grey sub-ice bedrock contours are descriptions of ice and underlying terrain, not named river courses. The northeastern fjord and land labels do not name the long modeled interior route.
correspondence.name_limit: Neither retained original establishes the complete route as one named surface river, one named subglacial river or one named glacier. Proximity to Danmark Fjord does not authorize a fjord-name transfer to a river, and a possible marginal watercourse cannot supply the identity of the entire ice-sheet route.
correspondence.conclusion: Readable coverage supports the completed geographical and feature-class scope review. Retain null names and no automatic application; a later assignment requires positive natural-river identity evidence.
correspondence.tributary_scope: The two displayed mainstem pieces cover the cached group; no additional tributary piece is present. This finding does not name other northeastern Greenland streams, glaciers or fjords.

scope_limit: MAIN_RIV groups and model mainstem roles do not establish a uniform name for every included reach, tributary or lake passage. Source observations support only the stated representative identity or hold.
publication_boundary: Own factual observations, attribution and official public URLs only; source originals, images, complete coordinates and private evidence remain omitted.
